name: AES Maximo solar installation robot
specialisedFor: utility-scale solar construction: lifting PV modules onto tracker torque tubes and tightening the clamps
summary: Tracked robot that lifts solar modules onto single-axis trackers with one robotic arm and tightens the clamps with a second, lower arm, guided by lidar and cameras. Developed by the power company AES and its incubated company Maximo and used on AES solar projects in the United States.

germany.statusNote: Not offered in Germany or the EU: Maximo is used on AES's own US solar projects (Oak Ridge in Louisiana, Cavalier, Bellefield in California). AES calls it construction equipment for EPC companies and developers, but no sale, rental or service offer outside the US was found.

specs.label: Crew
specs.conditions: one drives the system, one runs the machine
specs.quote: Maximo can be run by installation crews of two people.

specs.label: Installation rate
specs.value: more than one module per minute
specs.quote: Maximo’s version 3.0 units’ technical performance rate consistently surpassed one module per minute

specs.label: Modules per shift hour per person
specs.conditions: up to; Bellefield crews, about double traditional methods in the region
specs.quote: crews installing as many as 24 modules per shift hour per person

specs.label: Power source
specs.value: mobile microgrid with lithium iron phosphate batteries
specs.quote: Maximo runs on a mobile microgrid, using lithium-ion iron phosphate batteries as a power source.

specs.label: Sensors
specs.quote: Computer vision: Lidar and cameras provide spatial awareness for precise placement.

specs.label: Arms
specs.value: upper arm places panels, lower arm tightens clamps
specs.quote: A high-speed robotic arm performs the precise panel installation. The lower robotic arm tightens the clamps for fully automated installation.

specs.label: Units working in parallel at Bellefield
specs.quote: a coordinated fleet of four Maximo robot units operating in parallel

notes: Tracks for sandy, muddy and bumpy ground (maker).
Moved between rows with a human operator; a skid steer driver tows the robot (maker).
Stops when it detects people in the working area (maker).
Works with any solar module and a growing range of clamps, rails and trackers, at different torque-tube heights (maker).
